The correct sequential order of the reagents for the given reaction is :

4-nitroaniline $\longrightarrow$ 4-iodophenol
solution: Diazotise ($\text{HNO}_2$), replace by I (KI), reduce $-\text{NO}_2$ to $-\text{NH}_2$ (Fe/H$^+$), diazotise again ($\text{HNO}_2$), then hydrolyse ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$/warm) to the phenol.

stem: Which of the following mixing of 1 M base and 1 M acid leads to the largest increase in temperature?
solution: The more millimoles neutralised, the larger the temperature rise. (A) 30 mmol strong acid–strong base. (B) 30 mmol but a weak acid releases less heat. (C) 20 mmol. (D) 25 mmol. Hence (A).

Which of the following electronegativity order is incorrect?
solution: Pauling values: Mg 1.2, Al 1.5, B 2.0, N 3.0. The correct order is Mg < Al < B < N, so (A) is incorrect.

stem:
What will be the decreasing order of basic strength of the following conjugate bases?

$^-\text{OH}$, $\text{R}\bar{\text{O}}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}\bar{\text{O}}$, $\text{C}\bar{\text{l}}$
solution: Strong acids have weak conjugate bases. Acid strength: HCl > $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ > $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ > ROH, so base strength: $\text{Cl}^- < \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- < \text{OH}^- < \text{RO}^-$.

stem:
The increasing order of the acidity of the $\alpha$-hydrogen of the following compounds is :

(A) acetone, (B) 1,3-diphenylpropane-1,3-dione, (C) methyl acetate, (D) N,N-dimethylacetamide
solution: Cross-conjugation from N (amide) and O (ester) destabilises the carbanion; the 1,3-diketone gives the most stable anion. Order: D < C < A < B.
